The final answer 5816 is incorrect. It is not even a three-digit number, and it matches only the leftover quotient 727·8 = 5816 from an unfinished long-division step.

The proposed solution also has an indexing error. The digit a_k is floor(10·r_{k-1}/727), where r_k = 10^k mod 727, not floor(10·r_k/727). Using the correct indexing:

- r_725 = 10^{-1} mod 727 = 509, so a_726 = floor(5090/727) = 7 (since 727·7 = 5089, remainder 1).
- r_724 = 509² mod 727 = 269, so a_725 = floor(2690/727) = 3 (remainder 509).
- r_723 = 269·509 mod 727 = 245, so a_724 = floor(2450/727) = 3 (remainder 269).

The consistency checks hold: 10·269 ≡ 509 and 10·509 ≡ 1 (mod 727), and 10·1 = 10 gives a_1 = 0, matching the expansion 1/727 = 0.001375…. The last three digits of the repetend are therefore 3, 3, 7, which is **337**.
